questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: In JavaScript/TypeScript event loops, which queue has strictly higher priority immediately after the current synchronous call stack clears?

options.text: Macrotask Queue (`setTimeout(fn, 0)`) always runs before resolved Promises
CSS Repaint callbacks execute mid-function before return statements
`setInterval` preempts synchronous `for` loops
Microtask Queue (`Promise.then`, `queueMicrotask`, `MutationObserver`) runs completely before the next Macrotask (`setTimeout`)

questions.explanation: The JS runtime drains every queued microtask after each synchronous turn before picking up a single macrotask from the task queue.

`===` mutates compared variables into constants

questions.prompt: How does `Promise.allSettled()` differ from `Promise.all()`?

options.text: `Promise.all()` ignores rejected promises silently

`Promise.allSettled()` executes promises sequentially one by one

questions.prompt: Look at this TypeScript discriminated union handler. How can TS guarantee exhaustiveness at compile time if a new `status` case is added later?
questions.codeSnippet:
type State = { kind: 'ok'; data: string } | { kind: 'err'; error: Error };
function handle(s: State) { switch (s.kind) { case 'ok': return s.data; case 'err': return s.error.message; } }

options.text: Add a `default: const _exhaustive: never = s; return _exhaustive;` branch forcing compile errors on unhandled union cases
Cast `s as any` before switching
Disable `strict` in `tsconfig.json`
Use `typeof s === 'object'`

questions.explanation: Assigning unreachable `default` cases to `never` guarantees compile-time exhaustive checking when new union members are introduced.
